newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank revokes banking licence of BPG bank.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank revokes banking licence of BPG bank.

text.p: The president of the National Bank of Poland revoked on Monday the banking licence of the small Bank Powierniczo-Gwarancyjny SA and ordered its liquidation, the NBP said in a statement.
It said NBP's head Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz also asked the provincial Warsaw court to appoint a liquidator for BPG.
"The president of the NBP revoked the June 1, 1990 decision on granting permission to create Bank Powierniczo- Gwarancyjny SA," the NBP's press office statement said.

"At the same time the head of the NBP ordered the liquidation of BPG, which will be carried out according to the Commercial Code, and asked the Provincial Warsaw Court to appoint a liquidator," the statement said.
The NBP statement said the decision on the liquidation of BPG was read out to the bank's board, which refused to accept it, but which had immediate effect.

The bank said its decision was based on a ruling of the banking law, which says that the NBP may revoke a bank's licence and order its liquidation if the bank "notoriously does not comply with central bank rulings or its operation grossly violates the law or statute or endangers the interests of its depositors."
In February the central bank issued a statement indicating that BPG might have been involved in money-laundering and that its ownership structure was unclear.
No one at BPG was immediately available for comment.
